facts.text: On this date in 1002, King Æthelred II ordered the massacre of every Dane in England. The St. Brice's Day slaughter so enraged Danish king Sweyn Forkbeard that he eventually conquered the entire country.
On this date in 1956, the US Supreme Court ruled Alabama's bus segregation unconstitutional — ending the 381-day Montgomery Bus Boycott, the longest sustained urban protest in American history.
Mongolia has more horses than people. With 4.3 million residents and roughly 5 million horses, it is the only country on Earth where the livestock-to-human ratio tips in the horse's favor.
The city of Chongqing, China, is larger than Austria. Its municipality covers 82,000 sq km and holds 32 million people — more than Canada's three largest provinces combined.
More people live inside a 40km radius of Jakarta than in all of Australia. The Greater Jakarta metro area holds roughly 35 million people in a space smaller than Los Angeles County.

On this day in 1792, the first US federal building sold at public auction — Faneuil Hall in Boston fetched $250,000, a sum that would be worth roughly $8 million today, illustrating how slowly real estate appreciated before the 20th century.
On November 13, 1929 — two weeks after Black Tuesday — the Dow hit its post-crash low of 198. It would not fully recover for 25 years.
The global derivatives market notionally exceeds $600 trillion — roughly six times world GDP. Most of it exists purely to cancel out other bets.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway began as a failing textile mill. Buffett has called buying it the worst trade of his life, costing him an estimated $200 billion in opportunity cost.
Saudi Aramco paid out more in dividends in 2024 than Apple, Microsoft, and ExxonMobil combined — from a company most people cannot buy shares in.

On this date in 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet. It arrived at Mars to find the entire surface buried under a global dust storm — and simply waited for the skies to clear.
On this date in 1460, Johann Gutenberg lost his printing equipment to creditor Johann Fust. The man who invented the press that launched modernity died owning none of it.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body contains about 37 trillion cells, yet bacteria and other microbes on and inside you outnumber your own cells by a factor of roughly 1.3 to 1 — you are, by count, more microbial than human.
Light from the Sun takes 8 minutes to reach Earth, but the same photon spent up to 100,000 years fighting its way out from the Sun's core before it ever touched open space.
On this day in 1002, English king Æthelred ordered the massacre of all Danes in England. The St. Brice's Day Massacre helped trigger an invasion that made England a Danish kingdom within a decade.
On this day in 1940, Disney's Fantasia premiered — a film so technologically ambitious that most theaters had to install special sound equipment just to screen it.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the civilization Cortés destroyed by three centuries.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain could transmit images across a wire while most of the world had never heard a voice on one.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The ancient world was already ancient history to the ancient Egyptians.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or that never existed. English has no equivalent, which may say something unflattering about English.
Sonder (coined 2012): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. It spread so fast it now appears in some dictionaries, despite having a single invented source.

On this day in 1002, King Æthelred II ordered the killing of all Danes in England — an event named the St. Brice's Day Massacre. The Old English word 'nithling' (coward, villain) was likely coined for men who refused to carry it out.

On this day in 1833, the Leonid meteor storm rained roughly 100,000 meteors per hour over North America. The Cherokee called it 'the night the stars fell,' a phrase that anchored their oral calendar for a generation.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists have called it the most succinct word in any known language.

On Nov 13, 2017, Ethereum's Parity wallet was permanently frozen after a lone developer accidentally triggered a self-destruct function, locking ~514,000 ETH — funds that remain inaccessible to this day.

On Nov 13, 2020, Ethereum's Beacon Chain genesis block was finalized with 21,063 validators, crossing the 524,288 ETH deposit threshold needed to launch Proof-of-Stake — two years before the Merge made it canonical.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, was only activated in 2015. Before that, the nLockTime field existed in transactions but was entirely unenforced at the script level.
The Bitcoin whitepaper uses the word 'chain' only once. Satoshi's preferred term for the data structure was 'timechain' — 'blockchain' as a compound word was popularized later by the community.

Ethereum's EIP-1559 has permanently burned over 4 million ETH since August 2021. The burn rate is algorithmically tied to base fee, meaning network congestion directly reduces total supply in real time.

On this date in 2016, Google DeepMind published its AlphaGo Nature paper, formally documenting the first AI to defeat a professional Go player without handicap — a milestone most experts had placed a decade away.
On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica, a 120B-parameter science LLM, then pulled it after 72 hours when it confidently generated plausible-sounding but fabricated citations.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,600 average U.S. households.
The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every frontier AI system, was introduced in a 2017 paper by eight authors, most of whom left Google within two years of publishing it.

Chinchilla scaling laws, derived from a 2022 DeepMind study, showed that most large language models at the time were significantly undertrained relative to their parameter count — the field had been scaling parameters when it should have been scaling data.
